svg.aria-label: How Punc reads a book. A book comes from Project Gutenberg's most-read English books of the last 30 days, with Gutenberg's license header and footer cut off, or from your own plain text file, which is read in your browser and never uploaded. Punc folds the typography, so curly quotes become straight ones, long dashes become hyphens and an ellipsis becomes three periods. Then it counts the marks, period, comma, semicolon, colon, exclamation point, question mark, apostrophe, quotation mark, parentheses and hyphen, and keeps each one with its place in the book. Alice's Adventures in Wonderland drops 26,777 words and keeps 8,076 marks. The marks become four views: Score, every mark in reading order; Spiral, the whole book wound from the center out; Pages, the pages with the letters erased and the marks in place; and Counts, each mark through the book by tenth, with a fingerprint and the book's closest twin.
